overall_summary: Analysis across 37 unique videos shows extreme space exoplanets and high-stakes 'What If You Fell Into...' scenario hooks massively outperform all other categories, averaging 700-1,000+ views with high like ratios (3.5%-3.8%). In contrast, passive psychology facts ('Brain memories', 'Songs stuck in your head') and recycled concepts consistently flatline below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet' generated 1,029 views and 38 likes; 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice' reached 972 views; 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet' hit 824 views.
winning_patterns.action: Leverage immersive second-person POV ('You') experiencing catastrophic physical phenomena on bizarre celestial bodies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Physical Paradoxes in Planetary Science
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' achieved 981 views, 21 likes; 'Planet Darker Than Coal' got 1,031 views, 36 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight immediate, mind-bending scientific contradictions in the first sentence and title.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved between 5 and 53 views across multiple uploads; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' stalled at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause isolated brain trivia; shift psychology angles into high-stakes psychological survival or micro-horror mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads for 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' suffered severe algorithmic suppression (dropping from 220 to 34 views).
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate direct re-uploads; iterate on fresh entities and untapped mysteries rather than duplicating old scripts.
